summary.intent: Address CodeRabbit review comments on PR #372 (writable shares PoC), then extend the feature to support writable file shares (not just folder shares).
summary.outcome: All CodeRabbit threads resolved with fixes for: subfolder IPNS key management (new `folder-ipns` key type), shareKeysCache invalidation, missing 409 Swagger response, and doc correction. Writable file shares fully implemented with ShareDialog UI, recipient text-editor flow, shared key types, and E2E tests. Two follow-up CR threads resolved in a subsequent pass.

repo: Subfolder IPNS private keys in FolderEntry are ECIES-wrapped with the owner's public key — recipients cannot unwrap them directly; instead, recipients must self-wrap the key at subfolder creation time and store it as a `folder-ipns` share_key.
The `addShareKeys` write-recipient validation blocks `folder` keys (owner sets those) but intentionally allows `folder-ipns` keys (created and self-wrapped by the recipient).

The ShareDialog calls `sharesControllerCreateShare` directly (not share.service.ts's `createShare`) and already passes `permission` and `encryptedIpnsKey` — share.service.ts's createShare wrapper is a separate, lower-level abstraction.
CodeRabbit posts reviews both as formal review objects AND as issue comments; the review count can jump from 14 to 30 when a new review arrives.
Key types are validated with `@IsIn()` decorators in NestJS DTOs — centralising them in a `types.ts` with const arrays allows the same source to drive both TypeScript types and runtime validation.
The `ChildKeyDto` (used in create-share and invite flows) and `AddShareKeyDto` (used in addShareKeys) are separate types with overlapping but distinct allowed key type sets.
Schema drift CI checks compare the TypeORM entity column lengths against the current DB schema — adding `folder-ipns` (11 chars) to a varchar(10) column requires a migration.
The `fetchShareKeys` helper in share.service.ts had a hardcoded cast that silently dropped any key types not in the original union.

code.finding: useFolderNavigation unwraps subfolder IPNS key from folderEntry.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted using the owner's vault keypair — this field is owner-key-wrapped, unavailable to recipients.

When a recipient creates a subfolder, ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted in the FolderEntry is wrapped with the owner's public key only — no recipient-wrapped copy is stored unless explicitly added as a folder-ipns share_key.
Write operations guard on ipnsPrivateKeyRef.current being non-null — so if the key is zeroed on subfolder navigation, writes silently fail without crashing.
The addShareKeys validation blocks keyType === 'folder' for write recipients but folder-ipns is intentionally not blocked.
fetchShareKeys return type and internal cast only included file|folder|file-ipns, silently dropping folder-ipns keys introduced in this session.
New file: centralises ChildKeyType and ShareKeyType as const arrays + TypeScript union types, used by both @IsIn() validators and TypeScript type annotations across DTOs and entities.

workflow: When adding a new enum-like string value to a NestJS entity column, always check varchar length and generate a migration — the drift CI will catch it but it's faster to do proactively.
Regenerate the API client after every DTO change, not just at the end — cascading type errors are much harder to debug when multiple changes accumulate.
When a CodeRabbit review is still processing, polling with `gh api` for review count changes is effective; watch for the count to jump (14→30 in this case).
Reply to ALL review threads (including false positives) with reasoning before resolving — resolving without a comment can look like the comment was ignored.
For shared string union types used in both runtime validators and TypeScript types, `as const` arrays with a derived `typeof` type is the idiomatic NestJS pattern.

friction: CodeRabbit review took ~10+ minutes to post after acknowledging the request, requiring active polling loop.
API client regeneration needed to be run multiple times (after each DTO change) due to cascading type errors that only surfaced post-regeneration.
The `folder-only write` validation was added and then reverted mid-session after realising individual file write-shares are a valid use case — required cleanup of tests too.
TypeScript errors cascaded across invite DTOs, entities, controller, and the web invite service when widening the ChildKeyDto key type union.
The lint formatter rejected a `.then().catch()` chain that was too long — required manual reformatting.
Background task notifications arrived mid-session for already-completed work, requiring output file reads that added noise.
open_items: E2E tests for deep subfolder writes (8.2–8.5) and writable file shares are added but not yet run against a real environment — they cover new code paths that haven't been integration-tested.
Non-text writable file shares (images, PDFs) fall back to download — no edit UI for binary file write-shares.

Subfolder write access only works for subfolders created by the recipient in the current session — pre-existing subfolders created by the owner before the share was granted don't have a folder-ipns share_key for the recipient.
The `ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` on owner-created FolderEntries is owner-key-wrapped; a mechanism to re-wrap existing subfolder IPNS keys for new write-share recipients doesn't exist yet.
Migration `1743100000000-WidenShareKeyType.ts` created but not verified to run cleanly against all environments.
